slides.title: Some messages are tricks
slides.text: Some messages look friendly and exciting, but they are tricks. They want you to hurry, or to give away something private.
slides.alt: Spot the Trick opens its first message card: friendly words on the surface, and clues hiding in the text.

slides.title: Clues of a trick
slides.text: Look for clues. It says hurry, or it promises a prize you never tried to win. It asks for your passphrase. It comes from someone you do not know.
slides.alt: Checking the message: the first clue is marked, and the card still has more of its tricks to find.

slides.title: Trick or safe?
slides.text: This message has three clues: a surprise prize, a rush and a request for your key. It is a trick.
slides.alt: A second message card to judge: is it a trick with clues, or a safe message with none?

slides.title: What to do
slides.text: Real companies never ask for your passphrase. Do not reply or tap, and tell a trusted adult. A trick that fishes for secrets is called phishing.
slides.alt: A third trick card: the safe move is always the same — stop, do not reply, and tell a trusted adult.

slides.title: Secret codes for fun
slides.text: A cipher wheel turns letters into a secret code. Shift each letter by 3 and A becomes D. Only someone who knows the key can read it.
slides.alt: The cipher wheel: turn the key and every letter shifts, turning a plain message into a secret one.

words.means: a message that tries to fool you
a trick message that fishes for your secrets
a way to turn a message into a secret code
the secret that unlocks a code

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Spot the Trick and check 4 cards. Tap every clue you find, then choose. After that, crack a few secret messages with the key wheel.
slides.alt: Spot the Trick opens its first message card: friendly words on the surface, and clues hiding in the text.
